subject: Startups
title: The Remote Revolution
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Remote Revolution.

hook.text: In 2019, only 5% of jobs were remote. By 2021, it was 25%. The pandemic compressed a decade of change into months.

buildup.text: Remote work was once seen as a perk for freelancers. Suddenly it became survival mode for companies of every size.

discovery.text: GitLab built a $15 billion company with 1,500 employees across 65 countries—all fully remote from day one.

twist.text: Many founders say remote killed spontaneous collaboration. Others say it killed pointless meetings and commutes instead.

climax.text: Remote isn't a policy—it's an operating system. Companies that treat it as a temporary fix do it badly.

punchline.text: Remote works when it's designed, not just allowed.

quiz.question: What company built a $15B business fully remote from day one?
